body:
Set-up notifications : 
Code for testing :

```python
from notte.common.agent.types import AgentResponse
import asyncio
import os

# Create a sample AgentResponse
test_response = AgentResponse(
    answer="This is a test notification from Notte",
    success=True,
    env_trajectory=[],
    agent_trajectory=[],
    llm_usage=[],
    duration_in_s=1.5
)

# Test sending a notification
async def test():
    await notifier.notify(
        task="Test notification task",
        result=test_response
    )

# Run the test
await test()
```

Just have to change the notifier set-up.

```python
from notte.common.notifier.email import EmailConfig, EmailNotifier

config = EmailConfig(
    smtp_server=os.getenv("SMTP_SERVER"),
    smtp_port=int(os.getenv("SMTP_PORT", "587")), 
    sender_email=os.getenv("EMAIL_SENDER"),
    sender_password=os.getenv("EMAIL_PASSWORD"),
    receiver_email=os.getenv("EMAIL_RECEIVER")
)

notifier = EmailNotifier(config)
```

from notte.common.notifier.discord import DiscordConfig, DiscordNotifier

notifier: DiscordNotifier = DiscordNotifier(config)

title: Agent response in a mail
body: When asked, the response of the agent will be sent in a mail.
author: TonioSnowden

comments.body:
@TonioSnowden can you detail in this issue the API you want to develop so that we can agree on what it should look like before you implement this ? 

I was thinking or either designing external  modules, i.e

```python
result = agent(task=task, url=url)
if result.sucess:
  status = EmailClient(server_url).send(receipient_email="xyz@mydomain.com", result.answer)
```
=> user has to specific the email externally for this to work

Or a real email agent wrapper that does that directely from the task url prompt as we discussed

```python
# runs the tasks and sends the email in one single line
email_agent = EmailAgent(agent).run(task, url) 

class EmailAgent(BaseAgent)
     def __init__(self, base_agent: BaseAgent):
         pass

```
lets discuss and agree on this first @TonioSnowden

I would make it even more general with a `Notifier` component that can send messages on a number of channels eg Mail, Slack and Discord based on a flag. The flow is the same, only implementation of connectors change.

I was more on a different idea @giordano-lucas 

My vision was to add a parameter in the env of type `EmailConfig` : 

```python
class EmailConfig(BaseModel):
    """Configuration for email sending functionality."""
    smtp_server: str
    smtp_port: int = 587
    sender_email: str
    sender_password: str
    receiver_email: str
```

And you just pass it to the env and if there is a EmailConfig in the env it will send the response in a mail. Use the same idea as with the vault.

To follow the idea of @andreakiro I can set-up a abstract parent class Notifier. And then SlackConfig, MailConfig, DiscordConfig, ...

Because for me the env need to have the information of a potential Notifier class for long term vision. If we want to implement a prompt detection. i.e if the prompt is "send me by mail a daily update on the financial news of bitcoin" the env need to know if such a config exist.

This is a good start but 1) what if you want to send emails to a number of emails, or a number of slack channels? and 2) I am strongly opinionated against defining objects or too complicated objects in the `.env` We should have a system with a config file eg. `notte-config.yml` that stores all these things: notifiers, vaults, etc. The `.env` could point to the config address
